children: U.S. Senator Lummis said on the 20th that Democrats had previously called for the SEC to establish a dedicated office overseeing crypto certifications, but voted against a CLARITY Act provision creating one. According to Odaily, the September draft directed the SEC office to receive certification applications, assist with filings and refer them to the relevant departments for review. A list of 126 changes that Republican negotiators described as made at Democrats’ request placed the provision at No. 31; Democrats have not confirmed that account.

A procedural vote on September 15 failed to reach the 60-vote threshold, with the measure receiving 49 votes in favor and 50 against. Forty-four Democratic senators and four Republicans voted against it. Democratic Senator Gallego said negotiations over ethics provisions remained unresolved and questioned whether political donations from the crypto industry were receiving unequal treatment. Democrats are set to take control of Congress in January, making the CLARITY Act’s prospects more difficult.

title: CLARITY Act Provision Creating SEC Crypto Certification Office Draws Democratic Opposition
